subject: Intermittent SDK callback duplication with CycleHealth integration - coordination & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Cc: Ami Gupta <ami.gupta@cyclehealth.com>, Jared Mills <jared.mills@cyclehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent SDK callback duplication with CycleHealth integration - initial report

Hi team,

Bringing an issue from CycleHealth's POC that looks like SDK/runtime interaction causing duplicate downstream tool calls. Customer scenario: they call Redwood via our Node SDK (v1.3.2) with streaming enabled and a client-side callback that forwards certain tool calls to their worker. ~5% of requests result in the same tool being invoked twice within 200ms, leading to duplicate DB writes.

What I have so far: repro steps attached (repro_steps_cyclehealth.md) and a compressed trace of recent requests (request_trace_20261102.jsonl). Customer says it started after they upgraded to SDK 1.3.2 and switched to persistent connection mode.

Impact: POC blocked from moving to production - customer asked for timeline this week. They'd accept a short-term runtime config change if we can guarantee it doesn't regress other customers.

Ask: can runtime/platform triage root cause and advise a short-term mitigation we can apply to CycleHealth? Also: is there a quick SDK change we can ship (patch release) to reduce likelihood before a proper fix?

Proposed quick checks:
- confirm whether server-side dedupe by x-request-id is enabled for streaming requests
- check for duplicate KH (kernel handler) dispatch logs around those request timestamps
- confirm whether keep-alive/batch window changes correlate with duplication rate

I'll coordinate with the CycleHealth devs on any tracing we request.

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
loganw@redwood.com

Attachments: repro_steps_cyclehealth.md, request_trace_20261102.jsonl

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent SDK callback duplication with CycleHealth integration - initial report

Thanks Logan — I dug into the attached trace briefly. A few quick notes and requests: 

1) I can see repeated request_ids that look identical across two successful generation completions; that suggests the client retried without a new request-id or the server processed the stream twice.

2) Questions for the customer: can they confirm whether their callback ack is synchronous (blocking) or async (fire-and-forget)? If the client ack is slow, their worker might re-send.

3) Immediate triage items I need:
   - a single full raw request/response pair that includes headers (we need the x-request-id or any custom id they pass)
   - the SDK version (you noted 1.3.2) and whether they are using keepAlive: true in their HTTP client

Temporary mitigations we can try quickly (low-risk):
- Server-side: enable header-based dedupe for their tenant (enforce x-request-id dedupe for streaming sessions) — I can flip this flag on Dedicated or a customer-specific rule in config.
- Client-side: ask them to include a unique id per logical user action in X-Client-Action-Id and have their worker avoid reprocessing duplicates for 500ms.

I'll attempt a sandbox repro on our staging cluster; if I can reproduce, I can craft a narrow runtime patch.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Platform Engineer, Runtime

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent SDK callback duplication with CycleHealth integration - initial report

Quick triage notes from runtime perspective:

I reproduced a similar pattern in a local stress run when streaming + persistent connection + client-side callback that re-issues calls without explicit idempotency keys are combined. Two plausible failure modes:

A) Server-side race: if the streaming controller receives the same logical request (same client-supplied id) during a reconnect window it can enqueue two kernel dispatches before dedupe logic runs.

B) SDK behavior: older SDKs (<=1.3.2) do not automatically attach an x-request-id per user action; they rely on the transport layer. If keep-alive is true and the client restarts an internal send, the transport may reuse identifiers.

Short-term plan I can implement in staging today:
- Add a server-side dedupe layer for streaming sessions keyed on X-Request-ID + session-id with a 1s expiration (patch attached as server-side-dedupe-proposal.diff). This will be deployable as a canary for CycleHealth only.
- Parallel SDK mitigation: we should add a small patch to the Node SDK to auto-inject X-Request-ID (UUIDv4) for every logical request unless the user supplies one. I can provide a minimal patch proposal.

Risks: server dedupe may mask misbehaving clients; must be enabled per-tenant. SDK patch is low-risk and can be a minor release (1.3.3) with a note about idempotency header behavior.

I will start the server-side canary and post results.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachments: server-side-dedupe-proposal.diff

Thanks all — here's an action plan I propose to keep CycleHealth moving and keep scope tight:

1) Immediate (within 4 hours): Soojin flips tenant-scoped server-side dedupe for CycleHealth and we monitor for duplicate hits. Dev will run a targeted repro and confirm server dedupe catches the case. (Owners: Soojin / Dev)

2) Short-term SDK patch (24-48 hrs): Add auto-inject X-Request-ID in Node SDK 1.3.3, add test for streaming + keepAlive scenarios, and ship as minor. (Owner: SDK team — dev to coordinate with SDK maintainers)

3) Customer communication: Marissa/Logan to provide mitigations and updated timeline; offer a 25% POC credit for any impacted tokens if duplication caused extra processing. (Owner: Marissa)

4) Follow-up: If duplication persists after dedupe, open SUP-4821 to track deeper runtime race-fix and schedule a prioritized engineering ticket. (Owner: Dev)

Please confirm owners and timelines. Lauren — can you approve prioritization for ~6h of runtime engineering for the canary + up to 2 days for the SDK patch? Also asking permission to offer the token credit discussed to the customer to keep the deal moving.

Logan
